thinkers.name: Geoffrey Hinton

foresight: Early deep-learning conviction vindicated; radiology prediction failed; risk timelines unresolved.
allocation: Limited capital control, but large agenda-setting effect on governments and public.
contribution: Backprop popularization, Boltzmann machines, dropout, AlexNet.
corpus: Many dated interviews and talks, though often reported secondhand.
future: Nobel laureate whose risk warnings shape policy debate.

Nobel laureate; 10-20% extinction risk within ~30 years.

Urged Congress it has maybe a year to regulate before losing control.

assertions.claim: Large deep convolutional networks trained on GPUs with lots of labelled data can decisively beat hand-engineered computer vision (AlexNet, with Krizhevsky and Sutskever).
assumptions: GPU compute and ImageNet-scale data suffice to make deep nets outperform feature engineering
assertions.predictedOutcome: Deep neural networks become the dominant approach in vision and then other perception tasks.
assertions.contextAtTime: Neural nets were a minority approach in 2012 computer vision; SVMs and hand-crafted features dominated.
assertions.outcome: AlexNet won ILSVRC-2012 by a wide margin; deep learning became the dominant paradigm across AI and underpins all frontier models through 2026.
assertions.verdictRationale: The bet on large GPU-trained neural nets was contrarian in 2012 and was decisively vindicated.
assertions.evolution: Hinton's group was acquired by Google (DNNresearch, 2013); no revision of the core view.

assertions.claim: People should stop training radiologists now; it is completely obvious that within five years deep learning will do better than radiologists — it might be ten years.
assumptions: Image classification accuracy translates into replacing the radiologist's job
Regulation, liability and workflow would not slow substitution
Radiologists' work is mostly image reading
assertions.predictedOutcome: By ~2021 (at most ~2026) deep learning outperforms radiologists enough that training new radiologists is unnecessary.
assertions.contextAtTime: Deep CNNs had just surpassed humans on ImageNet classification (2015); early papers showed strong results on specific medical imaging tasks.
assertions.outcome: By 2025-26 the US and UK faced radiologist shortages; US average radiologist pay rose to ~$571k in 2025 (+9% y/y, Medscape) and case loads rose ~25% 2018-early 2025. AI tools are used as aids, not replacements; Mayo Clinic's radiology staff grew ~55% since 2016.
assertions.verdictRationale: Both the 5- and 10-year horizons have passed and demand for radiologists rose rather than fell. Task-level image accuracy gains were real, but the job-substitution inference ignored workflow, regulation and Jevons-like demand growth.
assertions.evolution: Reported to have later acknowledged he was off the mark (only weak LinkedIn-level evidence seen; NYT/Fortune revisited the claim in 2025-26). His 2025 job-loss warnings shifted to 'mundane intellectual labor' broadly.

assertions.claim: He was 'deeply suspicious' of back-propagation: 'My view is throw it all away and start again.'
assumptions: Brain-like (largely unsupervised) learning requires a mechanism other than backprop
Further progress needs a new learning algorithm
assertions.predictedOutcome: Progress toward more general AI would require replacing backprop-based training.
assertions.contextAtTime: Backprop-trained deep nets were dominant; Hinton was pursuing capsule networks (2017) and brain-inspired alternatives.
assertions.outcome: All frontier systems 2017-2026 (transformers, LLMs, reasoning models) remain backprop/gradient-descent trained; alternatives such as capsules and forward-forward have not displaced it.
assertions.verdictRationale: The subsequent decade of progress came entirely from scaling backprop-trained transformers; Hinton himself reversed in 2023, arguing backprop may be superior to the brain's learning.
assertions.evolution: Reversed by May 2023: concluded digital nets with backprop may learn better than biological brains, which became a basis for his risk concerns.

assertions.claim: Left Google to speak freely about AI dangers; revised his estimate for AI smarter than humans from '30 to 50 years or even longer away' to roughly 5 to 20 years.
assumptions: Capabilities of LLMs like GPT-4 continue to scale
Digital learning (weight sharing across copies, backprop) is more efficient than biological learning
assertions.predictedOutcome: AI broadly smarter than humans arrives roughly between 2028 and 2043.
assertions.contextAtTime: ChatGPT (Nov 2022) and GPT-4 (Mar 2023) had just shown rapid capability gains; the FLI pause letter had been published in March 2023.
assertions.outcome: As of Oct 2026 no consensus that AI is smarter than humans across the board; Hinton himself shortened the estimate further in 2025.
assertions.verdictRationale: Horizon extends to 2043; earliest bound (2028) not yet reached.
assertions.evolution: Shortened again by April 2025 to 'a good chance it'll be here in 10 years or less'.

assertions.claim: Estimated a 10% to 20% chance that AI leads to human extinction within about the next 30 years ('Not particularly, 10% to 20%' when asked if he had revised it).
assumptions: Superintelligent AI is built
Control/alignment is not solved
Competitive dynamics prevent a halt
assertions.predictedOutcome: A 10-20% probability of AI-caused human extinction or takeover over ~30 years.
assertions.contextAtTime: Made weeks after his Nobel Prize in Physics (Oct 2024); frontier labs racing on reasoning models.
assertions.outcome: No resolution possible as of Oct 2026; he repeated a 'sort of 10 to 20% chance' of AI taking control in April 2025.
assertions.verdictRationale: Probabilistic, long-horizon claim; not falsifiable by 2026.
assertions.evolution: Earlier cited ~10%; raised range to 10-20% and has kept it through 2025.

assertions.claim: On AI surpassing humans in every domain: 'there's a good chance it'll be here in 10 years or less.'
assumptions: Agentic AI and continued scaling keep improving capability
Competition among firms and nations prevents slowdown
assertions.predictedOutcome: Superintelligence (better than humans in every domain) plausibly by ~2035.
assertions.contextAtTime: Reasoning models (o1/o3, DeepSeek-R1) and agents had advanced rapidly in late 2024-early 2025.
assertions.outcome: Not resolvable by Oct 2026.
assertions.verdictRationale: Horizon not reached.
assertions.evolution: Further shortening of the 2023 5-20 year estimate; by Sept 2026 he told senators researchers' timelines were shortening.

assertions.claim: AI will replace 'everybody' in mundane intellectual labor; mass job displacement is more likely than not and already starting; physical trades are safer for a long time — 'a good bet would be to be a plumber'.
assumptions: AI capability in cognitive tasks continues to improve
Firms substitute rather than augment labor
Robotics/physical manipulation lags
assertions.predictedOutcome: Large-scale displacement of white-collar routine cognitive jobs (paralegals, call centers) before physical trades.
assertions.contextAtTime: 2025 saw CEO statements about AI replacing white-collar roles and early evidence of weaker entry-level hiring.
assertions.outcome: By 2026 Fortune reports layoffs had not spiked but evidence mounted of AI shrinking entry-level opportunities; no mass unemployment observed as of Oct 2026.
assertions.verdictRationale: No dated horizon; early signals are mixed. Note that his 2016 occupation-specific forecast (radiology) failed.
assertions.evolution: Generalizes the 2016 radiology claim into a broad labor claim.

assertions.claim: Told US senators that Congress has 'Maybe a year, but not much more than a year' to put guardrails on AI before it may be too late.
assumptions: Superintelligence timelines are shortening
Regulation must precede highly capable autonomous systems to be effective
assertions.predictedOutcome: If Congress does not act within roughly a year (by ~Sept 2027), effective control may be lost.
assertions.contextAtTime: Closed-door briefing convened by Sen. Sanders; House adjourned until after Nov 2026 midterms without AI legislation (single source).
assertions.outcome: Horizon not reached as of Oct 11, 2026.
assertions.verdictRationale: Deadline after the research cutoff.
assertions.evolution: Escalation of his post-2023 regulatory advocacy.

assertions.claim: If intelligence is a cake, unsupervised/predictive (later 'self-supervised') learning is the bulk of the cake, supervised learning the icing, and reinforcement learning the cherry.
assumptions: Most useful knowledge can be learned by predicting parts of raw data from other parts
assertions.predictedOutcome: Self-supervised learning on unlabelled data becomes the main source of AI capability.
assertions.contextAtTime: 2016 successes were mostly supervised (ImageNet) and RL (AlphaGo); self-supervised pretraining at scale was unproven.
assertions.outcome: Self-supervised next-token pretraining became the foundation of LLMs (GPT series, 2018-2026), with supervised fine-tuning and RL layered on top — though from 2024 RL for reasoning grew in importance.
assertions.verdictRationale: The core claim that self-supervised prediction would provide most of the learned knowledge was borne out — ironically via the autoregressive LLMs LeCun later criticized.
assertions.evolution: Retained; he later argued the self-supervision should be in representation space (JEPA) rather than generative token prediction.

assertions.claim: Autonomous machine intelligence requires learned world models trained by self-supervision in abstract representation space (H-JEPA), plus planning and objective-driven architecture, rather than generative models.
assumptions: Predicting in representation space avoids the intractability of predicting pixels/tokens
Physical-world understanding is a prerequisite for human-level AI
assertions.predictedOutcome: JEPA-style world models eventually outperform generative LLMs on the path to human-level AI.
assertions.contextAtTime: Published months before ChatGPT; LLM scaling was gaining momentum (GPT-3, PaLM).
assertions.outcome: Meta published I-JEPA (2023) and V-JEPA; LeCun founded AMI Labs (raised $1.03B, Mar 2026) to pursue it. As of Oct 2026 AMI had no product and reported results were not independently validated; LLMs remained dominant.
assertions.verdictRationale: Research programme with no deadline; neither vindicated nor falsified by Oct 2026.
assertions.evolution: No revision; became the basis of his 2025 departure from Meta.

assertions.claim: Auto-regressive LLMs are doomed: because each token carries some probability of error that compounds exponentially with answer length, they cannot be made factual, non-toxic or controllable without an architectural change.
assumptions: Per-token errors are independent and uncorrectable
Training can reduce but not eliminate the error rate
assertions.predictedOutcome: Autoregressive LLMs hit a reliability ceiling and are replaced by non-autoregressive, world-model-based systems.
assertions.contextAtTime: Weeks after ChatGPT/GPT-4 launches, amid widespread hallucination concerns.
assertions.outcome: By 2026 autoregressive LLMs remained dominant and improved markedly on long multi-step tasks via reasoning models that backtrack and self-correct within long chains of thought; hallucinations reduced but not eliminated.
assertions.verdictRationale: Reliability problems persisted as he said, but the specific mechanism (independent exponential error compounding) was undercut by models that correct their own errors, and LLMs were not abandoned. The ultimate 'no path to human-level AI' claim remains unresolved.
assertions.evolution: Repeated unchanged at NYU in Sept 2025.

assertions.claim: Fears that AI poses an existential risk are 'preposterous'; the debate is premature until there is a design for a system that can even rival a cat's learning ability.
assumptions: Current systems are far from animal-level intelligence
Objective-driven systems with guardrails will be controllable
assertions.predictedOutcome: AI will not pose an existential threat; safety will be engineered incrementally.
assertions.contextAtTime: Weeks after Hinton left Google and the CAIS extinction-risk statement signed by Hinton and Bengio.
assertions.outcome: No existential catastrophe as of Oct 2026; labs and Bengio-chaired International AI Safety Report document growing dangerous-capability and deception findings; debate unresolved.
assertions.verdictRationale: An opinion about long-run risk; absence of catastrophe to date does not falsify either side.
assertions.evolution: No revision found; repeated in WSJ (Oct 2024) as 'complete B.S.'.

assertions.claim: Open-source AI is safer and prevents concentration of power; calls by Altman, Hassabis and Amodei for regulation amount to attempted regulatory capture.
assumptions: Openness lets many actors find and fix flaws
Misuse risk from open weights is manageable
assertions.predictedOutcome: Open models will not cause catastrophic harm and will keep pace with closed ones.
assertions.contextAtTime: Meta had released Llama 2 (July 2023); the UK Bletchley summit and US executive order were imminent.
assertions.outcome: Open-weight models proliferated (Llama, DeepSeek, Qwen) and stayed close to the frontier; Meta itself became more cautious about open-sourcing its most capable models from mid-2025 (recalled). Hinton referenced a 2026 'Hugging Face incident' as a 'little Chernobyl' (details unverified).
assertions.verdictRationale: Normative claim; evidence cuts both ways and no decisive outcome by Oct 2026.
assertions.evolution: No revision found.

assertions.claim: 'on the path towards human-level intelligence, an LLM is basically an off-ramp, a distraction, a dead end' — while acknowledging LLMs are useful.
assumptions: Text-only training cannot yield physical-world understanding, persistent memory, reasoning and planning
assertions.predictedOutcome: Scaling LLMs will not reach human-level intelligence.
assertions.contextAtTime: GPT-4-class models widespread; heavy industry investment premised on scaling LLMs.
assertions.outcome: As of Oct 2026 no system is broadly accepted as human-level; LLM-based reasoning/agent systems kept improving and absorbed most investment.
assertions.verdictRationale: Not falsifiable until human-level AI is (or is not) reached by some route.
assertions.evolution: Hardened over time ('complete BS', Apr 2026).

assertions.claim: If Meta's research plan succeeds on schedule, within three to five years there will be systems of a completely different paradigm; within five years nobody in their right mind would use current LLMs as the central component of an AI system.
assumptions: JEPA/world-model research succeeds on the hoped timetable
assertions.predictedOutcome: By 2028-2030 a non-LLM architecture displaces LLMs as the core of AI systems.
assertions.contextAtTime: Similar 'passing fad' claim made at VivaTech June 2023; DeepSeek-R1 had just been released.
assertions.outcome: As of Oct 2026 LLMs remain central; AMI Labs had no product.
assertions.verdictRationale: Horizon (2028-2030) not reached; early trend does not favor it but cannot settle it.
assertions.evolution: Partly conditional on Meta's plan; after leaving Meta he moved the bet to AMI Labs.

assertions.claim: Left Meta after 12 years to found Advanced Machine Intelligence (AMI Labs) to build systems that understand the physical world, have persistent memory, reason and plan; raised $1.03B in March 2026.
assumptions: World models are the next paradigm
Capital can be raised for a non-LLM bet
assertions.predictedOutcome: AMI produces world models that outperform LLM approaches on physical-world tasks.
assertions.contextAtTime: Meta had reorganized AI under Superintelligence Labs (Alexandr Wang) focused on LLMs/products.
assertions.outcome: AMI raised $1.03B at $3.5B pre-money (Mar 2026); by Oct 2026 ~50-60 researchers, no product, results not independently verified.
assertions.verdictRationale: Too early to judge the venture.
assertions.evolution: Consistent with views held since 2022.

assertions.claim: Deep learning must move from 'System 1' pattern recognition to 'System 2' capabilities — reasoning, out-of-distribution generalization, compositional and causal representations.
assumptions: Current deep nets lack systematic generalization
New inductive biases/architectures are needed
assertions.predictedOutcome: Next major advances come from adding reasoning and causal structure to deep learning.
assertions.contextAtTime: GPT-2 era; scaling laws not yet published (Jan 2020).
assertions.outcome: Reasoning became the main frontier theme in 2024-2026 (o1/o3, DeepSeek-R1), but achieved mainly by RL-trained chain-of-thought on LLMs rather than the attention/causal-representation mechanisms he proposed; OOD generalization remains a weakness.
assertions.verdictRationale: Correct that reasoning would be the key gap; mechanism largely different from what he proposed.
assertions.evolution: Focus shifted from capability research to safety after 2023.

assertions.claim: Signed the FLI open letter calling for at least a six-month pause on training systems more powerful than GPT-4.
assumptions: Capabilities were outpacing safety and governance
A coordinated pause was achievable
assertions.predictedOutcome: A pause would allow safety protocols and governance to catch up.
assertions.contextAtTime: Days after GPT-4's release.
assertions.outcome: No pause occurred; labs continued training larger models (GPT-4o, Claude 3, Gemini, GPT-5).
assertions.verdictRationale: As an action aimed at achieving a pause, it failed; it did, however, help shift public debate (e.g., CAIS statement, Bletchley summit).
assertions.evolution: Moved toward institution-building (International AI Safety Report, LawZero).

assertions.claim: Revised his timeline: having placed human-level AI decades to centuries away, he now estimated roughly 5 to 20 years (with ~90% confidence), and warned that goal-directed superhuman AIs could go 'rogue'.
assumptions: Scaling plus modest algorithmic advances close the gap to human-level
Agency can be added to capable models
assertions.predictedOutcome: Human-level AI arrives roughly 2028-2043.
assertions.contextAtTime: Post-ChatGPT/GPT-4; Hinton made a similar revision the same month.
assertions.outcome: Not resolvable as of Oct 2026.
assertions.verdictRationale: Horizon not reached.
assertions.evolution: Maintained and intensified in 2024-2026 (International AI Safety Report, LawZero).

assertions.claim: Told the US Senate that human-level AI might come within a few years to a couple of decades and urged immediate regulation, licensing, and international coordination.
assumptions: Government action is feasible and effective in time
assertions.predictedOutcome: Binding national and international AI safety regulation needed quickly.
assertions.contextAtTime: Testified with Dario Amodei and Stuart Russell; EU AI Act under negotiation.
assertions.outcome: EU AI Act adopted (2024); no comprehensive US federal AI law as of Oct 2026 (Hinton's Sept 2026 briefing noted no legislation); international effort led to Bengio-chaired safety reports rather than binding treaties.
assertions.verdictRationale: Normative governance claim.
assertions.evolution: No revision found.

assertions.claim: As chair, delivered the first International AI Safety Report synthesising evidence on general-purpose AI capabilities and risks for governments.
assumptions: A shared scientific evidence base improves policy
assertions.predictedOutcome: An IPCC-like process informs international AI governance.
assertions.contextAtTime: Mandated at the Nov 2023 Bletchley Park summit; presented before the Feb 2025 Paris AI Action Summit, which shifted emphasis away from safety.
assertions.outcome: Report published; follow-up updates and a 2026 edition were produced (recalled).
assertions.verdictRationale: Institutional action; impact on policy not measurable yet.
assertions.evolution: Consistent with 2023 turn.

assertions.claim: Superintelligent agents pose catastrophic risks; a safer path is non-agentic 'Scientist AI' that models and explains the world without pursuing goals — launched LawZero (June 2025) to build it.
assumptions: Agency, not intelligence per se, drives the main risks
Non-agentic systems can be competitive and useful (e.g., as guardrails or for science)
assertions.predictedOutcome: A non-agentic Scientist AI can serve as a guardrail on agentic systems and accelerate science safely.
assertions.contextAtTime: Industry pivot to agents in 2025.
assertions.outcome: LawZero founded with ~$30M (recalled); no deployed Scientist AI as of Oct 2026 found.
assertions.verdictRationale: Research agenda with no deadline.
assertions.evolution: Builds on his 2023 conversion; opposite bet to industry's agent focus.

assertions.claim: Frontier models already display deception, cheating and self-preservation behaviours in tests — early warning signs of loss-of-control risk.
assumptions: Behaviours in contrived evaluations indicate dispositions that matter in deployment
assertions.predictedOutcome: Such behaviours will become more capable and consequential as agency grows unless addressed.
assertions.contextAtTime: Apollo Research scheming evaluations (Dec 2024) and lab system cards reported such behaviours.
assertions.outcome: Multiple evaluations documented scheming/deception in test scenarios; no major real-world loss-of-control incident confirmed (a 2026 'Hugging Face incident' referenced by Hinton is unverified here).
assertions.verdictRationale: The empirical claim that such behaviours appear in evaluations is supported; the implication about real-world danger is not yet testable.
assertions.evolution: No revision found.

assertions.claim: If you have a large dataset and you train a very big neural network, success is guaranteed (seq2seq-era statement of the scaling hypothesis).
assumptions: Large networks trained on enough data can learn any function needed
Compute will keep growing
assertions.predictedOutcome: Bigger networks on more data will continue to deliver breakthroughs.
assertions.contextAtTime: Following AlexNet (2012) and seq2seq translation (2014); mainstream ML still favored smaller models and hand-designed structure.
assertions.outcome: Scaling became the dominant strategy from GPT-2/GPT-3 (2019-2020) through GPT-4 and beyond; scaling laws formalised the trend.
assertions.verdictRationale: An early, contrarian conviction that was strongly vindicated over 2017-2024.
assertions.evolution: Qualified in Dec 2024 ('pretraining as we know it will end') and Nov 2025 ('age of research').

assertions.claim: Co-founded OpenAI as chief scientist to pursue AGI.
assumptions: AGI is achievable via scaled deep learning
A mission-driven lab can lead
assertions.predictedOutcome: OpenAI becomes a leading AGI lab.
assertions.contextAtTime: Left Google Brain; OpenAI launched as a non-profit with ~$1B in pledges.
assertions.outcome: OpenAI produced GPT-3, ChatGPT and GPT-4, becoming the leading commercial AI lab.
assertions.verdictRationale: The lab he co-founded became central to the field.
assertions.evolution: Left in May 2024.

assertions.claim: Predicting the next token well requires understanding the underlying reality that produced the text — compression is understanding.
assumptions: Good compression of data requires modelling its generative process
assertions.predictedOutcome: Better next-token predictors will exhibit increasingly genuine understanding and reasoning.
assertions.contextAtTime: Post-GPT-4; directly opposed by LeCun and Marcus who argued LLMs lack understanding.
assertions.outcome: LLM capability on reasoning benchmarks rose sharply 2023-2026, but much of the gain came from RL post-training rather than pretraining alone; debate over 'understanding' remains open, and Sutskever himself stressed a generalization gap in 2025.
assertions.verdictRationale: Philosophical/technical claim not settled by evidence to date.
assertions.evolution: By Nov 2025 emphasised that models generalize dramatically worse than people.

assertions.claim: Co-led OpenAI's Superalignment team with the goal of solving the core technical challenges of superintelligence alignment within four years, backed by 20% of OpenAI's secured compute.
assumptions: Superintelligence could arrive within the decade
Automated alignment researchers can be built
assertions.predictedOutcome: Core superintelligence alignment problems solved by mid-2027.
assertions.contextAtTime: Corporate OpenAI announcement co-authored with Jan Leike.
assertions.outcome: The team was dissolved in May 2024 after Sutskever and Leike left OpenAI; the four-year horizon has not elapsed.
assertions.verdictRationale: Deadline (2027) not reached, though the programme as constituted ended early.
assertions.evolution: Continued the safety-first goal at SSI.

assertions.claim: As an OpenAI board member, voted to remove Sam Altman as CEO; days later said he deeply regretted participating in the board's actions.
assumptions: Board oversight could constrain leadership in service of the non-profit mission
assertions.predictedOutcome: Leadership change at OpenAI.
assertions.contextAtTime: Tension between commercialization and safety at OpenAI.
assertions.outcome: Altman was reinstated within five days after employee revolt; Sutskever left the board and departed OpenAI in May 2024.
assertions.verdictRationale: The action failed to achieve its aim and was reversed within days.
assertions.evolution: Publicly reversed (regret post, Nov 20, 2023).

assertions.claim: Founded Safe Superintelligence Inc. as a 'straight-shot' lab with one goal and one product — safe superintelligence — insulated from short-term commercial pressure.
assumptions: Superintelligence is reachable by a small focused team with a different research approach
Investors will fund years without product revenue
assertions.predictedOutcome: SSI develops safe superintelligence without intermediate products.
assertions.contextAtTime: Weeks after leaving OpenAI.
assertions.outcome: SSI raised ~$1B (Sept 2024) and was reportedly valued ~$32B (Apr 2025); co-founder Daniel Gross left for Meta (July 2025) and Sutskever became CEO. No public product found as of Oct 2026 (unverified for Jul-Oct 2026).
assertions.verdictRationale: Venture outcome not yet determinable.
assertions.evolution: Consistent with Superalignment-era priorities.

assertions.claim: Pre-training as we know it will unquestionably end: compute keeps growing but data does not — 'we have but one internet'; data is the fossil fuel of AI. Future systems will be agentic, reason, and be less predictable.
assumptions: High-quality human-generated data is finite
Returns from pure pretraining scale diminish
assertions.predictedOutcome: Labs shift emphasis from scaling pretraining to new axes (reasoning, synthetic data, agents, inference compute).
assertions.contextAtTime: Reports in late 2024 of disappointing returns from next-gen pretraining runs; o1 had shown reasoning gains.
assertions.outcome: 2025-2026 frontier progress came largely from RL-based reasoning, inference-time compute and agents; GPT-4.5 (Feb 2025) was seen as showing diminishing pretraining returns. Pretraining nonetheless continued at larger scale and was not abandoned.
assertions.verdictRationale: Direction (shift to reasoning/agents, data as constraint) proved right; 'end' of pretraining did not occur literally by 2026.
assertions.evolution: Extended in Nov 2025 into 'age of research' framing — a revision of his 2014-era 'scale guarantees success' view.

assertions.claim: 2020-2025 was the 'age of scaling'; we are back in an 'age of research, just with big computers'. Models generalize dramatically worse than people; systems that learn as well as humans could come in roughly 5 to 20 years.
assumptions: Scaling current recipes yields diminishing returns
A new learning approach can close the generalization gap
assertions.predictedOutcome: Next breakthroughs come from new ideas rather than more scale; human-like learners in 5-20 years.
assertions.contextAtTime: Industry capex at record levels premised partly on continued scaling; reasoning-model gains continuing.
assertions.outcome: Not resolvable as of Oct 2026.
assertions.verdictRationale: Long horizon.
assertions.evolution: Reversal relative to his earlier scaling maximalism.

assertions.claim: Deep learning faces ten fundamental challenges (data hunger, poor transfer, lack of hierarchical structure, weak open-ended inference, opacity, poor integration of prior knowledge, correlation vs causation, etc.) and must be supplemented by other (symbolic) techniques to reach general intelligence.
assumptions: Scale alone cannot overcome these limits
assertions.predictedOutcome: Pure deep learning stalls short of general intelligence; hybrids needed.
assertions.contextAtTime: Just before GPT-1/BERT (2018) and the pretraining revolution.
assertions.outcome: Several challenges (data efficiency, reliability, OOD generalization) remain open; others (transfer, open-ended language inference) improved dramatically through scale. Tool use and code execution in LLM agents add some symbolic components.
assertions.verdictRationale: Correctly flagged persistent weaknesses but underestimated how much scale would solve.
assertions.evolution: Consistent; restated repeatedly 2019-2026.

assertions.claim: Deep learning is hitting a wall: scaling will not deliver reliability or understanding; neurosymbolic approaches are needed.
assumptions: Scaling yields diminishing returns on reasoning and reliability
assertions.predictedOutcome: Near-term scaled models would show limited progress on reasoning/reliability.
assertions.contextAtTime: Pre-ChatGPT; GPT-3 and early PaLM existed; scaling laws widely accepted.
assertions.outcome: ChatGPT (Nov 2022), GPT-4 (Mar 2023) and reasoning models (2024-2025) delivered large measured gains on reasoning and professional benchmarks and massive adoption; hallucinations and reliability issues persisted.
assertions.verdictRationale: Measured capabilities rose steeply in the following years, contradicting a 'wall' in 2022; his reliability concerns were partly valid but do not rescue the headline claim.
assertions.evolution: Re-asserted in Nov 2024 ('diminishing returns') after pretraining slowdown reports.

assertions.claim: Offered Elon Musk a bet that AGI would not arrive by 2029, under specified criteria.
assumptions: Current approaches lack robust understanding
assertions.predictedOutcome: No AGI meeting his criteria by end of 2029.
assertions.contextAtTime: Musk had said he expected AGI by 2029.
assertions.outcome: Not resolvable as of Oct 2026.
assertions.verdictRationale: Deadline not reached.
assertions.evolution: No revision found.

assertions.claim: Testified to the US Senate (alongside Sam Altman) calling for an FDA-like licensing agency, independent audits and international oversight of AI.
assumptions: Self-regulation by AI companies is insufficient
assertions.predictedOutcome: Strong external regulation is needed to manage AI risks.
assertions.contextAtTime: First major congressional AI hearing after ChatGPT.
assertions.outcome: No US federal AI licensing agency as of Oct 2026; EU AI Act adopted.
assertions.verdictRationale: Normative claim.
assertions.evolution: Later grew more critical of OpenAI/Altman (2024 book 'Taming Silicon Valley').

assertions.claim: For 2024: roughly 7-10 GPT-4-level models; no massive advance (no GPT-5-level model); price wars; little moat; no robust solution to hallucinations; modest corporate adoption and profits.
assumptions: Scaling returns slowing
Many labs could replicate GPT-4
assertions.predictedOutcome: By end-2024: multiple GPT-4-class peers, no GPT-5, falling prices.
assertions.contextAtTime: Gemini announced Dec 2023; Claude 2/Llama 2 below GPT-4; widespread expectation of GPT-5 in 2024.
assertions.outcome: 2024 saw many GPT-4-class models (Claude 3/3.5, Gemini 1.5, Llama 3.1 405B, Qwen, DeepSeek-V2/V3), steep API price cuts, no GPT-5 (released Aug 2025), and persistent hallucinations. OpenAI's o1 (Sept 2024) was a notable reasoning advance some would call a substantial leap.
assertions.verdictRationale: Most specific components held by end-2024; the o1 reasoning jump is the main caveat.
assertions.evolution: Issued follow-on predictions for 2025.

assertions.claim: Generative AI could turn out to be an economic 'dud' — its value far below what valuations implied — and the boom resembles a bubble.
assumptions: Hallucinations limit enterprise adoption
Revenue will not justify capex
assertions.predictedOutcome: Disappointing revenue relative to investment and a correction in AI valuations.
assertions.contextAtTime: Mid-2023 hype after ChatGPT; capex ramp beginning.
assertions.outcome: Through mid-2026 AI capex and lab revenues kept growing rapidly; no broad AI market crash had occurred as of the last verified information (Jul-Oct 2026 not verified). Enterprise ROI evidence remained mixed.
assertions.verdictRationale: No deadline; a bubble cannot be confirmed or refuted until a cycle completes.
assertions.evolution: Repeated through 2024-2025.

assertions.claim: GPT-5 was overdue, overhyped and underwhelming; hallucinations and reasoning errors remain unsolved in pure LLMs.
assumptions: LLMs lack world models and robust reasoning
assertions.predictedOutcome: LLM scaling will not eliminate hallucinations.
assertions.contextAtTime: GPT-5 released Aug 7, 2025 to mixed reviews.
assertions.outcome: Hallucinations reduced but not eliminated as of 2026; OpenAI researchers acknowledged structural incentives behind them (Sept 2025).
assertions.verdictRationale: Persistence of hallucinations supports him; 'underwhelming' is a judgment, and GPT-5 class models were widely used.
assertions.evolution: No revision found.

relations.note: Sutskever was Hinton's PhD student and co-authored AlexNet with him and Krizhevsky.

LeCun publicly dismissed the existential-risk concerns Hinton raised after leaving Google, calling AI doom fears 'preposterous'; later headlines report LeCun 'rejects Hinton' while calling LLMs a dead end.
LeCun disputed Bengio's catastrophic-risk arguments and calls for regulation; in Oct 2023 criticized 'Turing awardees' backing restrictions (AI Business headline).
Both revised AI timelines in May 2023 and signed the CAIS extinction-risk statement.
LeCun accused Altman (with Hassabis and Amodei) of attempting regulatory capture.
LeCun accused Amodei/Anthropic of lobbying to restrict open source (regulatory capture).
Named alongside Altman and Amodei in LeCun's regulatory-capture accusation.
As Meta's chief AI scientist LeCun championed the open-weights Llama strategy that Zuckerberg endorsed; they diverged in 2025 when Meta reorganised around Superintelligence Labs and LeCun left.
Proposed H-JEPA world models (2022) and founded AMI Labs (2025-26) to build them.
Sutskever voted with the OpenAI board to remove Altman as CEO, then said he regretted it.
Co-founded SSI with Daniel Gross and Daniel Levy; CEO since July 2025.
Moved from 'big network + big data = guaranteed success' (2014) to 'pretraining will end' (2024) and 'age of research' (2025).
Testified alongside Altman at the May 2023 Senate hearing and has since been a persistent critic of OpenAI and Altman.

Long-running public dispute: Marcus argues LeCun dismissed his critiques of deep learning and later adopted similar conclusions about LLM limits; they agree LLMs are insufficient for human-level AI but disagree on remedies (neurosymbolic vs JEPA) and on AI risk/regulation.
Offered Musk a bet that AGI would not arrive by 2029.

Marcus's 'diminishing returns' and 'wall' claims are the opposite of Sutskever's earlier scaling conviction; after Sutskever's NeurIPS 2024 'peak data' talk and Nov 2025 'age of research' remarks, the two converge on the view that pure scaling is insufficient.
From 'throw it all away and start again' (2017) to viewing backprop-trained digital nets as potentially superior to brains (2023).
Founded LawZero to build non-agentic Scientist AI.
Both signed the FLI pause letter (recalled).
Testified together at the July 2023 Senate hearing in favour of AI regulation (recalled).
